1.explanation_en: 关 means “lock”; 起来 marks the resulting state of being shut in. Here it does not mean “get up.”
即 + 位 (“assume” + “position”) is a compact expression for taking the imperial position, hence acceding to the throne.
过 means “pass,” and 了 marks the passage as complete; together they introduce the elapsed time 一会儿 (“a while”).

1.meaning_en: was more than ten zhang in length
1.explanation_en: 有 introduces the extent; 十多丈 gives a length exceeding ten zhang, and 长 identifies length as the dimension. The passage gives no modern conversion for 丈.
下 (literally “send down”) combines with 诏 (noun, edict) in the compact expression for issuing an edict.
变 (verb, become) takes 雄 (adjective, male) as the resulting state. Here 雄 describes the chicken’s sex; it is not the noun in 雄鸡, “rooster.”
看 means “read,” and 后 follows the event to mark that what comes next happens after the reading; 后 is not an aspect marker.
看 is the verb “read”; 了 marks the reading as completed before the memorial is passed on.
结 means “join” or “bind,” while 在一起 describes the resulting state of being together; together they express forming a group.
被 marks the passive, and 称为 means “call” or “designate as”; together they say that the subject receives a name or designation.
考 means “take an exam,” and 中 is the result complement meaning the attempt succeeded. 的 marks the phrase as a modifier referring to a person; the negation 没 lies outside this unit in the sentence.
聚集 means to gather or assemble; the neutral-tone aspect marker 了 marks the gathering as a completed event.
成 is the verb “become,” and the neutral-tone 了 marks the resulting state as having come about; the following phrase names that state.

1.meaning_en: to establish ties with; associate with
1.explanation_en: 结 means to form, and 交 here refers to association; together they make a verb for establishing a relationship.
杀 is “kill”; attached 了 marks the action as completed.
关 means to shut or confine, and 进 is a directional complement indicating movement into a place. The destination 牢里 remains separate.
裹 means to wrap, and 着 marks the resulting state as continuing. Together they describe something remaining wrapped around the person.
引出 combines 引, ‘draw or bring,’ with 出, which presents someone as brought forth; 了 marks the event as completed.
做官 means serving in an official role; 官 names that role generally, without specifying a rank. The experiential 过 marks having done this before.
听 names the event, and 后 places the following reaction after that event; it does not mark aspect on 听.
看 means “read” or “look at”; 了 marks this act as completed and attaches to the predicate.
有 (“have”) takes 志 as a noun meaning “aspiration” or “resolve”; together they describe having ambition.
出 means “put forth,” and 力 is the noun “strength” or “effort”; together they form the reusable expression “exert effort.”
看 means “look at” or “read”; attached 着 presents the action as ongoing while Liu Bei sighs.
像 introduces the comparison, and 一样 marks similarity to 雷 (“thunder”); together 像 X 一样 is a reusable pattern for “like X.”
推 is the verb “push”; 着 is a neutral-tone aspect marker that presents the pushing as ongoing or in progress.
杀 is the verb “kill”; attached 了 marks the killing as a completed event.
结为 means “form or become as”; 兄弟 names the resulting relationship, so together they describe forming a bond as brothers.
结为 means to form or become a status, and 兄弟 names that status: they enter a brotherly relationship.
同 means “same” and 心 here means “intention”; together they express having a shared purpose, not merely having the same heart.
祭 is “perform a sacrifice”; the result complement 罢 marks that action as finished, setting up what happens next.
带 means “bring” and 着 presents the accompanying state: the companions are with the guests as they arrive.
赶 means “drive or urge along”; 着 presents that action as ongoing while they bring the group of horses.
听 is the verb “hear”; 后 follows it to mark the time after that event.

1.meaning_en: regard Liu Bei as a nephew
1.explanation_en: 认…为… presents someone as having a particular identity or role: 认 means “regard/recognize,” and 为 introduces the role assigned.
没过 with a duration means that the time span has not elapsed; 几天 supplies that span. Here 过 means “elapse,” not “pass by” a place.
Here 将领 is a compound noun for a military commander. 将 is read jiàng in this role, not jiāng as the word for “will” or “be going to.”
来 indicates movement toward the place in the narrative, and 犯 supplies the attack or incursion; together they describe an attack coming toward that place.
围 means “wrap around”; the attached state marker 着 presents the wrapping as a continuing state.
出 means “go out,” and 战 means “fight”; together they form a compact verb for going out to engage in battle.
翻 means “turn,” and 身 means “body”; together they form the compact verb 翻身, describing a turn of the body.
落 means “fall,” and 马 identifies the horse; together 落马 is a compact expression for falling from horseback.
斩 means “cut down”; 成 marks the resulting state, and 两段 specifies that the result consists of two sections.
展现 means “display” or “show,” and 了 marks the completed event. Together they form the predicate; 了 does not include the following object.
守 means “defend” or “hold,” 不 marks inability in this potential construction, and 住 supplies the sense of holding or maintaining the position. Here 不 is unstressed and neutral-toned.
迎 (verb, meet or face) + 战 (noun, battle) combines facing an opponent with engaging in battle.
退 (verb, retreat) + 后 (direction, back) form one predicate describing movement toward the rear.
扎 (verb, pitch or establish) + 营 (noun, camp) describe establishing a camp.
出 (verb, go out or bring forth) + 兵 (noun, troops) form a compact military expression for deploying troops.
解开 (verb, loosen or undo) describes removing the encirclement; attached 了 marks the completed change.
交 (verb, engage) + 战 (noun, battle) form a compact expression for opposing sides fighting one another.
赶 means to hurry, and 路 here refers to the journey being made; together they describe traveling in haste, rather than hurrying a physical road.
交 combines with 战 to form a compact verb for opposing sides entering combat; here 交 does not mean to hand something over.
带 means to take or lead along, and the attached aspect marker 着 presents that accompanying action or state as continuing while they escape.
骗 means to deceive, and 过 is a result complement meaning to get past someone; here it is not the experience marker 过.
相信 means to believe, and the aspect particle 了 marks the act as having occurred. Here 了 is not a separate change-of-state marker.
举 means to recommend, and 为 introduces the resulting status, 孝廉. The passive context comes from 被 before this unit.
做 means to take on or serve in a role here, and the aspect particle 了 marks that action as having occurred; the role itself follows.
带 is the verb “lead/take,” and 着 marks the accompanying state as continuing while they retreat.
逃 is “escape”; 了 marks the event as completed, and 出去 adds movement outward. Together they describe getting out by escaping.
带 is the verb “take/bring,” and 着 marks the accompanying state as continuing while they travel.
带 means “take” or “lead”; attached 着 presents the taking along as ongoing or as an accompanying state while Liu Bei returns. The names that follow remain separate.
押 is the verb “escort under guard”; 回 is a directional complement indicating movement back toward a reference point.
听 means “listen,” and 完 is a result complement showing that the listening reaches completion.
押 means “escort under guard”; 走 is a directional complement indicating departure. 被 marks the passive construction outside this unit.

1.meaning_en: charge at a gallop, moving away
1.explanation_en: 飞马冲 describes charging at a gallop; 去 is the directional complement, indicating movement away from the reference point. In this connected predicate use, 去 is unstressed and pronounced qu.
救 means “rescue,” and 下 is a result complement marking that the rescue is achieved. Here 下 is grammaticalized and unstressed, pronounced xia.
得 introduces a degree complement: 不得了 intensifies 气, “anger,” to an extreme degree. In this construction 不得了 means “extremely,” not “unable to.”
